I could not answer the question. Falkon found the repository and its `src` tree, but I have no tool that reads commit history, so I could not tell which merged PRs since 2026-04-16 added or removed a `voidedValue` line. My tools here are grep, glob, read_file, list_tree, list_repos and symbol lookups. None of them lists commits, PRs or diffs, and reading `.git/logs/HEAD` failed because Falkon does not expose `.git`. Nothing in the repository was modified.

What I did establish is the current state of `voidedValue` under `src` at the default branch. Falkon has no pinned head for this repo, so I could not restrict to the main line up to it. The repo is `github.com/openmrs/openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib` (the bare name `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib` did not resolve). The 61 matches in 10 files break down as follows:

- **Type definition:** `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib/src/types/schema.ts` line 122 declares `voidedValue?: any` on the submission type.
- **Helper that sets it:** `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib/src/utils/common-utils.ts` lines 33–52 define the default `voidedValue: null`, `gracefullySetSubmission(field, newValue, voidedValue)`, and the check for a voided value.
- **Encounter payload building:** `openmrs-esm-form-engine-lib/src/processors/encounter/encounter-processor-helper.ts` lines 245–298 and 436–437 read `voidedValue` to build obs for submission.
- **Tests:** the remaining matches are in `*.test.ts` and `*.golden.test.ts` files under `src/adapters`, `src/processors/encounter` and `src/provider`. They assert on or construct `voidedValue` but do not change the answer about which PRs touched it.

To get the PR list, the next step is a history tool such as `list_commits` (on the default branch, up to the pinned head) plus `get_diff` for each commit since 2026-04-16. Those were named in Falkon's instructions but are not among the tools I have in this session. With them, I would filter commits whose diff adds or removes a line matching `voidedValue` in `src`, then map each commit to its merged PR and merge date.
